content:
HubSpot Company Record — QuillForge AI (quillforge.ai)

Summary
- AI-native startup building an in-product coding assistant + repo Q&A for mid-size engineering orgs.
- Strong PLG motion: self-serve signup, wants clear proof points they can forward to eng + finance ("latency per dollar" resonates).
- Primary interest: Redwood Hosted API for chat + embeddings; exploring Dedicated if they hit sustained >200 RPS.

Buying stage / temperature
- Stage: Evaluation
- Current posture: positive on product + docs, but skeptical of marketing benchmarks unless they can reproduce quickly.
- Quote (lead eng): “If you can show me p95 under load and the unit economics aren’t a science project, we’ll switch.”

Key contacts (from notes)
- Priya S. (Head of Eng) — cares about p95 latency, model pinning, rollback/fallback.
- Marco D. (Platform Eng) — cares about routing headers/regions and SDK ergonomics.
- Alex K. (Finance/ops) — cares about predictability, spend caps, cost attribution.

Workload / technical requirements
- Workloads:
  - Chat completions (streaming) for code assistant; mix of short prompts + occasional long-context (8–16k) summaries.
  - Embeddings for doc-search (index updates daily + query-time embeddings).
- Performance targets (stated):
  - Chat: p95 < 900ms time-to-first-token at moderate concurrency; stable under peak concurrency spikes during US work hours.
  - Embeddings: consistent throughput during batch indexing; wants predictable $/1M tokens.
- Model preferences:
  - Open models preferred; want ability to pin model version for releases and do canary rollout.
  - Needs documented fallback behavior (if region capacity constrained, how does it degrade?).
- Region:
  - Mostly NA users today; EU roadmap in H2.
  - Asked specifically about cross-region differences and whether they can “lock to us-east until we’re ready.”

Economic requirements / objections
- Wants Hosted API performance proof beyond a single headline number:
  - asks for p50/p95 + throughput and how latency/$ is computed.
  - wants confidence intervals / variance language; suspicious of cherry-picking.
- Objections heard:
  - “Benchmarks don’t match my traffic mix.”
  - “Variance / noisy neighbors — what’s your rerun policy?”
  - “How do I reproduce without burning a week?”
  - “Can you cap spend and provide per-route cost breakdown?”

Security / compliance
- Not blocked on enterprise security today, but asks for:
  - SOC 2 (for larger customers they sell into)
  - audit logs / request tracing controls (at least basic)
  - retention controls (don’t want prompts stored beyond a short window)

Lifecycle / marketing ops
- Enrolled in lifecycle email sequence: Benchmark Report Nurture (PLG)
  - Segment: high-intent (visited pricing + docs; downloaded report)
  - UTM tracking: benchmark_report_launch / nurture_touch_1
- Notes: they are receptive to benchmark content, but only if it includes constraints/disclaimers and “how to replicate” guidance.

Recent activity timeline
- 2025-01-28 — Inbound signup + product usage started (Hosted API trial).
- 2025-02-03 — Priya requested “performance proof” to justify switching from incumbent (notes mention Together.ai).
- 2025-02-06 — Discovery call (Fireflies ff-2d71c-quillforge-discovery-2025-02-06). Focus: p95 under concurrency + unit economics.
- 2025-02-07 — Stephanie emailed benchmark overview + offered to share methodology appendix + reproduction snippet.
- 2025-02-14 — Sent benchmark report link w/ UTMs; added note to call out NA region tables + hosted API CTAs.
- 2025-02-18 — Markus looped in for technical eval; answered questions on model pinning, fallback policy, and regional routing headers.
- 2025-02-21 — Priya requested a “mini-repro plan” using their own prompt set (20–30 prompts) and concurrency ramp.

Next steps (proposed plan)
- Provide a lightweight reproduction checklist (their prompts + our recommended concurrency distribution; capture p50/p95 + throughput + cost per 1M tokens).
- Markus to advise on:
  - batching/caching defaults appropriate for their mix
  - region selection + model pinning during rollout
  - what variance to expect and how to interpret it
- Stephanie to keep them in nurture but add 1:1 follow-up after touch #2 (methodology deep dive).

Internal notes
- This account is very PLG-friendly: wants docs, numbers, and a clean “engineer-to-engineer” story.
- Best angle: production economics + reproducibility + transparency (avoid absolute superiority claims).
- Watch-out: if we can’t clearly explain variance + region differences, they’ll default back to incumbent due to perceived risk.
